ui.siteFull: Pilgrimage of the Grand Priory of Bohemia of the Order of Malta to Lourdes
ui.kicker: The Order’s pilgrimage with the sick
ui.heroLead: Every spring, the sick, volunteers and pilgrims of the Grand Priory of Bohemia of the Order of Malta travel to Our Lady of Lourdes. We fly together on a special flight from Prague, and in Lourdes we join the Order’s international pilgrimage, which brings together some 10,000 people from all over the world.

ucast.title: Taking part
ucast.description: How to apply for the Order’s pilgrimage to Lourdes, how to pay and how to contact us.
ucast.body:
If this information has caught your interest and you would like to join us on the pilgrimage, please proceed as follows:

  1. Send your applicationChoose the application form for your group on the Applications page.
  2. Wait to hear from usWe will let you know whether you have a place on the pilgrimage and send you your personal payment reference (variable symbol).
  3. Pay for the pilgrimageTo account no. {account} (IBAN {iban}), quoting the payment reference you have been given.
  4. Practical instructionsIn good time, you will receive further information about the flight and the pilgrimage programme.

If you would like to take part in the pilgrimage, send your completed application straight away. Even so, all places may already be taken and we may not be able to accept your application. Please believe us that this is not ill will on our part and that we do our very best to accommodate as many people as possible. Please wait until we send you a message or get in touch with you.

Practical instructions

Based on our experience from previous years and given the amount of work involved in organising the pilgrimage, we have had to take the following measures:

  • we do not send application forms by post; they can be downloaded from this website or filled in online,
  • send completed application forms by email to {email} or by post to {post}; please mark the envelope clearly “Lurdy”,
  • we will send you all further information by email,
  • please do not telephone the offices of the Grand Priory of Bohemia or of Maltézská pomoc; neither of them is involved in organising the pilgrimage and they cannot give detailed information,
  • please contact us by email only, at {email}.

We understand that this may cause difficulties for many of you, but without these measures the situation would be unmanageable for us. Please ask your friends or family to help you with email.

prihlasky.title: Applications
prihlasky.description: Application forms for the Order’s pilgrimage to Lourdes for the sick, pilgrims and team members.
prihlasky.body:
To apply for the pilgrimage, please proceed as follows:

  1. Choose your groupA sick person staying at the Accueil (mainly wheelchair users and the seriously ill), a sick person staying at the hotel (sick people who can walk), a healthy pilgrim staying at the hotel, or a team member.
  2. Fill in the applicationChoose the right application form below and fill it in online, or download it and send it by email or post.
  3. Wait for our replyAs soon as possible, we will send you detailed information about payment, the departure date and the rest of the arrangements.

Consent to the processing of personal data

By applying for the pilgrimage, you consent to Maltézský nadační fond LOURDES processing the personal data given in your application, including data about your health and health care, for the purpose of organising the pilgrimage. After the pilgrimage, personal data may be processed only for statistical and archival purposes. You will find more details in the privacy policy.

By submitting an application, you declare that you are aware that false or incomplete information about your state of health may cause complications or put your life at risk, and you take full responsibility for this.

faq: Why do members of the Order of Malta go to Lourdes and care for the sick there?

Since its foundation in the 11th century, one of the Order’s priorities, alongside the defence of the faith, has been caring for the sick and the suffering. Members of the Order gave them the care and help they needed, always at the best level available at the time. From the very beginning, the Knights of Malta have also had a great devotion to Our Lady.

In Lourdes, these two sides of the life of the Order’s members come together. We go on pilgrimage to Lourdes to honour Our Lady, and at the same time we care for the sick and the suffering, and not only physically. In Lourdes, too, following the Order’s tradition, we try to give the best possible care and comfort to the sick, whom the Knights of Malta have for centuries called “our lords the sick”.

For all the members of our “great Maltese family”, it is always a joy to meet others from different countries. Some 10,000 members and volunteers of the Order come to Lourdes every year, and it is encouraging for us to know that we belong to a great family with a thousand-year tradition.
Why does the team’s uniform say “BOHEMIA”?

Our pilgrimage is organised by the Grand Priory of Bohemia of the Order of Malta, in French Grand Prieuré de Bohême. Bohemia is the Latin name for the Lands of the Bohemian Crown. The Grand Priory of Bohemia is one of the oldest in the world and has existed without interruption since its foundation. Out of respect for this tradition, all members of our group, whatever their nationality, wear the BOHEMIA badge on their uniform.
What luggage should I take?

It is best to pack your things in one suitcase and one smaller piece of hand luggage. Hand luggage must comply with airport security rules: it must not contain a knife, scissors or any other sharp objects, however small, or liquids. These are confiscated without exception at the security check.

Do not forget to bring enough of all the medicines you take.
What weather should I expect, and what should I wear?

Bring clothes for both warm and cold weather and for rain, as the weather in Lourdes is unpredictable. We recommend several layers that can be combined or taken off (for example a woollen jumper), and a hat for both sun and rain. If you use a wheelchair, a rain cover for the wheelchair is also useful.
How does air travel work with a wheelchair?

A pilgrim in a wheelchair is checked in at the airport together with the wheelchair and, with the help of their assistant from the Maltese team, goes in it right up to the plane. Specialist airport staff help them on board, and the wheelchair is stowed in the hold. After landing, everything happens the same way in reverse.
Why is it not possible to travel with an electric wheelchair?

Airlines do not want this for safety reasons. Even with individual permission, the captain may refuse to carry such a wheelchair. In Lourdes, too, an electric wheelchair would be more of a complication, given the local traffic and organisation.
Who will look after our luggage?

When you arrive at the airport, report to the designated members of the organising team; they will be clearly identifiable. You will receive labels for your luggage, wheelchair and anything else you are taking with you. Everything must be marked with these labels, even if you already have your own; the labels follow a system that helps the organisers handle the luggage.

You will also receive a name badge to wear around your neck with your name, where you are staying, the name of our group and the contact details of your group’s organiser. The organising team looks after the luggage from check-in at the airport until it arrives at the hotel.
Are meals provided during the journey?
Normal refreshments are served on board during the flight. Diabetics should arrange it with us in advance and take the dose of insulin they need on the plane.
Where will we stay?

Accommodation is provided at a hotel or at the Accueil. You will find a detailed description in the travel information. The luggage labels have different colours depending on where you are staying, so it is essential that every piece of luggage carries the label you receive from the organisers.
What are the rooms like?

At the Accueil there are rooms with two, three and six beds, completely barrier-free, with a bathroom and toilet. All bed linen and the necessary nursing equipment are provided. At the hotel there are rooms with two and three beds, with a bathroom and toilet, bed linen and towels.
What about meals in Lourdes?

Everyone has full board where they are staying (hotel or Accueil). A continental breakfast, and lunch and dinner of several courses, are usually served. We will provide special diets according to the information in your application.
How will the programme in Lourdes be organised?

We are all taking part in the international pilgrimage of the Order of Malta, so we follow the common programme; you will find details in the booklet you receive at the airport. We will go to some places all together, and at other times we will split into smaller groups. You will be given the details on the spot.
What happens at the baths?

The baths, fed by the spring from the Grotto, are well organised. Everything is run by local volunteers, and assistants help in the water. You do not need your own swimwear; you will be given a cloth to cover yourself when you are immersed. Everything takes place calmly and with dignity, and the assistants are very considerate.
What should priests bring?
For concelebration, priests should bring a Czech missal, an alb and a stole. Everything else needed to celebrate Holy Mass is available on site.
Will it be possible to attend Holy Mass every day?

Holy Mass is planned for every day. Changes are possible on the days of arrival and departure, when everything depends on the journey and the weather.

If anything seems confusing, please bear in mind that all times had to be booked in Lourdes a year in advance and the organisers in Lourdes have to coordinate the requests of all the groups.
Can I take Lourdes water home?
Near the rock there are special taps from which pilgrims can fill their own containers with as much water as they like. Bottles of all sizes can be bought on site.
Should we take out insurance for the journey?

Czech health insurance guarantees necessary health care in the European Union. However, what counts as necessary care differs from country to country, and many things have to be paid for. In any case, the journey is safer with travel insurance.
Where can I buy souvenirs of Lourdes?

There are many shops in Lourdes selling all kinds of souvenirs. They are outside the Sanctuary, so they do not disturb the services in any way. The shops are barrier-free, and the sick will also have enough time to shop with the help of their assistants.

The priests accompanying our pilgrimage can bless religious articles for you; everything will certainly be blessed at the end of the pilgrimage.

gallery.lead: Photos and short reports from previous years.
gallery.2003: Our first pilgrimage of our own in the modern history of Maltézská pomoc. 11 sick people and 13 team members went on pilgrimage to Lourdes. The group was accompanied by the Order’s chaplains Fr Jiří Jeřábek and Fr František Hofman. As in many years to come, the pilgrimage was led by Bettina and Jiří Lobkowicz. We took a scheduled flight to Paris, crossed Paris by coach and travelled on to Lourdes by TGV high-speed train.
gallery.2004: 16 sick people and 20 team members went on pilgrimage to Lourdes, and the group was accompanied by a chaplain of the Order. Once again we took a scheduled flight to Paris, a coach took us across Paris, and we continued by TGV high-speed train. Although the journey was physically and financially demanding, we had many beautiful moments, which we remember fondly.
gallery.2005: For the first time we flew directly from Prague to Lourdes on a special flight, which we shared with a Polish group. 20 sick people travelled with us, cared for by 30 team members. The group was accompanied by the Order’s chaplain Fr F. Hofman, Fra’ Norbert Kinský and the Grand Prior, Fra’ Karel Paar. The temperature in Lourdes reached 30 °C that year.
gallery.2006: Once again we flew on a special flight shared with a Polish group. 23 sick people travelled with us, cared for by 29 team members. The group again included the Grand Prior, Fra’ Karel Paar, Fra’ Norbert Kinský, the Order’s chaplains and a deacon.
gallery.2007: We took a scheduled flight to Paris and from there a coach all the way to Lourdes. 18 sick people travelled with us, cared for by 27 team members. Near Toulouse, two of our coach’s tyres burst and we waited five hours for the mechanic. This trial too was made up for by unforgettable experiences in Lourdes.
gallery.2008: The 150th anniversary of the apparitions of Our Lady in Lourdes and the 50th pilgrimage of the Order of Malta. For the first time, we sent a special plane of our own from the Czech Republic. On board were 40 sick people, 55 team members and 65 pilgrims. The group was accompanied by Mgr Jiří Paďour and Mgr Dominik Duka, the Grand Prior, Fra’ Karel Paar, Fra’ Pierre de Bizemont, the Order’s chaplains and many other priests.
gallery.2009: For the second time, we sent a whole special plane from the Czech Republic directly to Lourdes. For the first time, the pilgrimage was led on their own by Ursula and Tomáš Czernin. 32 sick people travelled with us, along with 36 team members including two priests, and 100 pilgrims together with the entire leadership of the Grand Priory of Bohemia.
gallery.2010: The group numbered 29 sick people, 42 members of the care team and 95 other pilgrims, 166 people in all. In the Year for Priests, and thanks to the support of the Cesta 121 movement, 20 priests took part in the pilgrimage, 12 of them of advanced age.
gallery.2011: The Order’s 53rd pilgrimage to Lourdes took place from 28 April to 2 May 2011. From the Grand Priory of Bohemia, 30 of our lords the sick took part, cared for by 55 volunteers in Maltese uniforms. All the remaining seats on the plane were taken by pilgrims.
gallery.2012: The Order’s 54th pilgrimage to Lourdes took place from 3 to 7 May 2012. From the Grand Priory of Bohemia, 34 of our lords the sick took part, cared for by 49 volunteers, together with 77 pilgrims.
gallery.2013: The Order’s 55th pilgrimage, from 2 to 6 May 2013, was attended by 33 of our lords the sick, 56 members of the care team and 94 pilgrims. Our group gave thanks with a generous collection to repair the damage caused by the floods that hit Lourdes twice that year.
gallery.2014: The Order’s 56th pilgrimage, from 1 to 5 May 2014, was attended by 32 of our lords the sick, helped by 51 members of the care team, and 106 pilgrims.
gallery.2015: The Order’s 57th pilgrimage, from 30 April to 4 May 2015, was attended by 30 of our lords the sick, helped by 52 members of the care team, and 107 pilgrims.
gallery.2016: The Order’s 58th pilgrimage took place from 28 April to 2 May 2016. 50 members of the volunteer team cared for 26 of our lords the sick, who were accompanied by 109 pilgrims.
gallery.2017: The Order’s 59th pilgrimage took place from 4 to 8 May 2017. Once again a full plane took part, 189 people: 35 of our lords the sick, 49 volunteers and 105 pilgrims. The presence of Cardinal Dominik Duka was a great honour for everyone.
gallery.2018: The Order’s 60th pilgrimage took place from 3 to 7 May 2018. The plane was full again, with 189 pilgrims: 35 of our lords the sick, cared for by 58 volunteers, and 99 independent pilgrims. The pilgrims were accompanied by two deacons and 9 priests, including the Bishop of Ostrava-Opava, František Václav Lobkowicz, and his brother, the Abbot of Teplá, Filip Zdeněk Lobkowicz.
gallery.2019: The Order’s 61st pilgrimage took place from 2 to 6 May 2019. It was attended by 192 pilgrims: 104 pilgrims staying at the hotel and 34 of our lords the sick, cared for by 54 volunteers. The pilgrims were accompanied by 8 priests, including Bishop František Václav Lobkowicz and Abbot Filip Zdeněk Lobkowicz.

privacyBody:
Controller

The controller of personal data is {controller} (Maltese Foundation Fund LOURDES), company ID (IČO) {ico}, with its registered office at {seat}, registered in the Register of Foundations kept by the Municipal Court in Prague under file no. N 751. Please send questions and requests concerning personal data to {email}.

Applications for the pilgrimage

We process the data from your application (name, date of birth, contact details, identity document details, the contact details of a family member and, for the sick, of their general practitioner) so that we can organise the pilgrimage: give you a place on the pilgrimage, arrange your plane ticket and accommodation, and agree on payment. The legal basis is the performance of the contract for participation in the pilgrimage (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR).

We process data about your health, medicines, diet, allergies and the care you need only with your explicit consent (Article 9(2)(a) GDPR), so that we can provide you with safe care, suitable accommodation and meals during the pilgrimage. You can withdraw your consent at any time by email; withdrawal does not affect processing carried out before it, but without these data we cannot ensure your safe participation.

The data are seen only by those members of the pilgrimage organising team who need them and, to the extent necessary, by the airline, the accommodation providers and the Sanctuary of Lourdes. After the pilgrimage, we keep the data only for statistical and archival purposes; we delete the data about your health once the pilgrimage is over.

The online application is sent in encrypted form and delivered by email through the Resend service (Resend, Inc., USA), which sends emails for us as a processor. The website does not store the application. We send to the email address given in the application only a confirmation that it has been received, without any data from the application.

Cookies and visitor statistics

This website does not use cookies or any analytics or advertising tools, and it does not track visitors. Fonts and images are loaded directly from this website.

Website hosting

The website runs on servers of Vercel Inc. (USA). On every visit, the data needed to deliver the page and to protect the website against misuse are processed (IP address, time and address of the request, browser information). The legal basis is our legitimate interest in the secure operation of the website (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR). Transfers to the USA are governed by the EU–US Data Privacy Framework or by standard contractual clauses.

Your rights

You have the right of access to your personal data, the right to have them rectified or erased, the right to restriction of processing and the right to data portability, the right to withdraw your consent and the right to object to processing based on legitimate interest. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Office for Personal Data Protection (Úřad pro ochranu osobních údajů), Pplk. Sochora 27, 170 00 Praha 7, uoou.gov.cz.

Last updated: 18 October 2026.
